correctness.rationale: For all finite simple edge-transitive graphs with at least one edge, trace(AB)=2m and trace-norm duality give the lower bound. Edge-orbit invariance of U=I-2P_negative(A), together with trace(AU)=trace|A|, forces U_edge=energy/(2m)>0 and produces a feasible matching upper bound with U squared equal to I. Zero eigenvalues and complex Hermitian completions are covered. Root-of-unity Fourier averaging and a uniform absolutely summable expansion prove all three cycle correction constants; supplementary script tests passed.

value.rationale: This exactly solves a natural spectral-norm completion invariant on the full edge-transitive graph class by a constructive spectral-sign involution, including infinitely many cycles where the original adjacency is suboptimal. It links graph energy to an optimization objective and obtains nontrivial modulo-four sharp asymptotics. It is a structural classification rather than an arbitrary finite sample or routine recomputation of known cases.
